claims.explanation: Promazine is a phenothiazine that inhibits MALT1 protease and blocks biogenic amine uptake, and its selective killing likely reflects dependence on MALT1/NF-kB signaling or monoamine/lysosomal pathways rather than a single lineage. The strongest genomic predictors are activating EGFR mutations and TP53/CDKN2A alterations, which are enriched in sensitive lung and aerodigestive lines, while BRAF/NRAS-mutant melanomas and several KRAS-mutant gastrointestinal lines are relatively resistant. Expression of MALT1, NFKB1, and monoamine-handling genes such as SLC6A2/SLC6A4 may further refine sensitivity.

features.basis: Enriched in sensitive NSCLC lines (NCIH1650, HCC4006, KYSE270); EGFR-driven lines may depend on NF-kB/MALT1 survival signaling
TP53 mutations are common across most sensitive lines and may impair apoptotic compensation to phenothiazine stress
Observed in sensitive SNU1214 and other sensitive lines; cell-cycle deregulation may increase dependence on survival pathways
Promazine inhibits MALT1 protease; high MALT1 expression/activity predicts dependence on MALT1-NF-kB signaling
MALT1 inhibition blocks anti-apoptotic NF-kB signaling; active NF-kB pathway predicts sensitivity
BRAF-mutant melanomas (UACC62 sensitive but IPC298, IGR37, K029AX resistant) show mixed but overall less consistent killing; BRAF-driven MAPK survival may protect
NRAS-mutant IPC298 and KU1919 show resistance or only moderate sensitivity; RAS/MAPK activation may buffer phenothiazine stress
KRAS-mutant pancreatic and colorectal lines (SNU410, T3M4, CL11) are among least affected
Promazine blocks norepinephrine uptake; high SLC6A2 expression may increase intracellular drug exposure or monoamine-mediated toxicity
Promazine and similar phenothiazines interact with serotonin uptake; SLC6A4 expression may modulate sensitivity
CYP2A6 metabolizes promazine; high expression may reduce active drug levels and protect lines
Promazine is a dopamine receptor antagonist; DRD2 expression may mediate direct growth-inhibitory or survival effects
